results.name: Band Low Chest Press
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point above head height. Step one foot in front and the other back, with both knees slightly bent, facing away of the anchor point, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing down, positioning your hands near to your shoulders.
Press both handles forward until your arm is fully extended. Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement, then slowly return the handles to the starting position with control.
Repeat the pressing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the band handles forward and inhale as you return it back.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Focus on using your chest muscles to press the band handles.
results.description: Band Low Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Palloff Press
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand perpendicular to the anchor point, holding the handle of the band with both hands close to your chest.
Push the band straight out in front of you, extending your arms fully and squeezing your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return your hands to your chest, maintaining control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning towards or away from the anchor point.
Engage your core to resist the rotational pull of the band.
Adjust the band’s tension or your distance from the anchor for an appropriate challenge.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push the band forward and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Band Palloff Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with the resistance band crossed around your upper back and each end secured under your hands, which should be placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your feet should be together.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Band Push-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Core.

results.name: Band Single Arm Pec Fly
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handle of the band in your working hand with your arm extended out to the side, palm facing forward.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your chest engaged.
Pull the band in an arc motion, bringing your hand towards the center of your chest.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement.
Use a controlled motion to pull and return the band, preventing any jerking movements.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band across your body and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbow slightly bent throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
results.description: Band Single Arm Pec Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Barbell Bench Press Decline
instructions: Set a decline bench at a suitable angle and lie down on it with your feet secured under the foot pads. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet secured under the foot pads to maintain stability and prevent sliding.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Bench Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View)
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45 degree angle and lie down on it with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Bench Press (Side View)
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar with control to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Press it back up to full extension and repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades squeezed and your upper back tight.
Use a spotter for heavy sets.
results.description: Barbell Bench Press (Side View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and position the bar directly above your chest.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Floor Chest Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your feet flat on the floor. Grip a barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms bent, elbows on the floor.
Engage your core and slowly press the barbell up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position by bending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your elbows are at a 45-degree angle to your body to reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
results.description: Barbell Floor Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent, feet resting on the bench, and grasp the barbell at a grip wider than shoulder width. Position the bar over the middle of your chest.
Lower the barbell slowly toward your mid chest by bending your elbows while keeping your wrists straight and shoulder blades retracted.
Press the barbell upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight without locking them forcefully.
Pause briefly at the top, then repeat while maintaining a controlled tempo throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pressed firmly into the bench, engaging your core for stability.
Maintain a neutral wrist position throughout the lift.
Lower the bar to the middle of your chest in a controlled manner.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Serratus Anterior.
